newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia students say punish police brutality.
newsitem.headline: Serbia students say punish police brutality.

text.p: Belgrade students demanded on Monday that President Slobodan Milosevic pull back his feared police and punish those who ordered an attack on demonstrators on Sunday night or tender his resignation.

"Holding you personally responsible for the institutional and brutal violence used against the peaceful demonstrators in the night between February 2 and 3, 1997 with which you have once again shown that you do not act as a president of all citizens of the Republic of Serbia

"We demand from you to immediately order urgent withdrawal of all police forces blocking peaceful demonstrations, to urgently determine the responsiblity of all persons involved in making and implementing decisions concerning the use of violence and institute proceedings for their punishment.
"If you are unable to do so we demand that you immediately resign," the students said in their letter to Milosevic.

The letter was released after Milosevic's dreaded security police with batons, water cannon and gas attacked peaceful protesters overnight, injuring some 150 people in the worst political violence seen for years in Belgrade.
The students have backed opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition demands for Milosevic to hand back their victory at November 17 local election in 14 Serbian cities, including Belgrade.
But they have not so far demanded Milosevic's resignation and the letter is bound to raise more tensions.
The Socialist-dominated government signed a statement with the students last month agreeing to meet all their demands but so far has not kept its promise.
In another letter to the government, the students "resolutely demand the dismissal of Serbian interior minister over the events that happened in Belgrade."
They also called for those responsible for ordering the use of water cannon and tear gas and brutal beating of citizens in peaceful demonstrations to be identified and punished.

"The brutality of the police and desperation of the regime can be gauged from the fact that police even stormed the Faculty of Philosophy and beat students, which never happened during the 1968 protest," said Vesna Pesic, one of the three Zajedno leaders who was beaten herself.
Witnesses spoke of unusual police brutality in their unprecedented charge into the faculty and student leaders said they will retaliate but did not specify how.

"We were witnesses to the brutal police behaviour directed from the top. We shall not allow such beatings and abuse and our answer will be appropriate. By this I announce the students will take more radical measures," Dusan Vasiljevic, the student protest spokesman, told Reuters.
Doctors from a private clinic which has set up emergency quarters at the Faculty of Philosophy said 85 students were treated for injuries.
Two students were standing up against a wall with hands in the air while seven or eight police beat them, witnesses said.
"When they fell the students were not allowed to help them and then they were put into a police van," one said.
